[UNCLEAR: the source opens with the phrase “ten figures.”] It describes figures along the path of the Sun, namely the twelve zodiac signs. Among them are three hundred and sixty stars in twenty-one figures inclined away from the Sun’s path toward the north. These include the Great Bear, the Lesser Bear, the Dragon, and others. Among them are three hundred and sixteen stars in fifteen figures inclined away from the Sun’s path. [UNCLEAR: the source’s statement about how the named stars were classified by the practitioners is difficult to parse.]

Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Jabbār, known from his book [UNCLEAR: the title appears as “al-Baṣrah”] on the fixed stars, mentioned them and said: The stars in the northern figures include the Lesser Bear. It resembles a standing bear stretching out its paws. It has seven stars, and the Arabs call it the Lesser Banāt Naʿsh. Four stars form the bier in a square, and three lie on its tail. Eight stars lie outside the figure. Among them are seven stars that the Arabs classify as the Lesser Banāt Naʿsh, the stars observed toward the North Pole. [UNCLEAR: the source’s overlapping seven- and eight-star descriptions are retained as stated.]

I say: Among them is the Great Bear, with twenty-seven stars. Eight stars lie outside the figure. Among them are seven stars that the Arabs call Banāt Naʿsh: four on its body and three on its tail. The Arabs call them al-Suhā. Among them is the Dragon, with thirty-one stars. Its figure is a great serpent with many coils. It begins with four stars arranged as an inclined square at its head. [UNCLEAR: the source’s phrase following the head-and-scorpion description is garbled.] The Dragon is a place in the heaven, a kind of serpent, and the greatest of them.

Among them is al-Fakkah, called the Northern Crown. [UNCLEAR: the source gives a garbled description of a kind of heavenly serpent and eight stars associated with its roundness.] Al-Fakkah also consists of round stars behind al-Simāk al-Rāmiḥ.

Among them is the Kneeling Man, whose figure has twenty-seven stars. Among them are al-Sabʿāt, also called al-Lawz and al-Ṣubḥ al-Rūmī. Among them is the Tortoise, whose stars number ten; some of its stars are drawn as al-Nasr al-Wāqiʿ. There is also the Hen, which has nineteen stars; two stars lie outside the figure, and its largest stars are in the Milky Way. Among them is the Triangle, four stars between the star of the Fish and the Eagle above the head of al-Ghūl. Thus the total of these northern figures is three hundred and sixty stars.

As for the southern figures, they comprise three hundred and twelve stars. Among them is [UNCLEAR: Qayqaṭus], with twenty-two stars. Its figure is a bare animal with two legs and a tail like the tail of a whale. Among them is al-Jabbār (Orion), with thirty-eight stars. Its figure is a running man holding a staff, with a belt and a sword at his middle. Among its stars is al-Jawzāʾ, a red star. There are also twelve stars gathered beneath Orion’s leg, resembling a rabbit whose face is toward the west and whose rear is toward the east.

Among them is the Great Dog, with twenty-eight stars; eleven stars lie outside the figure, behind the stars of al-Jawzāʾ. [UNCLEAR: the source’s relation between al-Sunbulah and the stars of al-Shiʿrā al-ʿAbūr is obscure; it calls one al-Abbān al-Marzabān.] Among them is al-Shiʿrā al-Ghumaysāʾ, the stars that rise after al-Jawzāʾ. As for Cancer, [UNCLEAR: the source refers to figures in al-Jawzāʾ and to al-Shiʿrā al-Ghumaysāʾ in the arm]. The Arabs claim that the two are the sisters of Suhayl.

Among them is the Southern Crown, with thirteen stars; six stars lie outside the figure. Its figure is a great fish, with its stars south of the star al-Dālī, its head toward the east and its tail toward the west. Among them is the Milky Way, [UNCLEAR: the source’s location phrase is garbled]. This is a summary of the southern and northern stars.

I say: What some authors have mentioned is restricted to the famous stars. As for the less famous stars, they are very numerous; they will be mentioned later, if God Most High wills.

[UNCLEAR: sumber membuka dengan frasa “sepuluh gambar”.] Sumber menjelaskan gambar-gambar di sepanjang jalan Matahari, yaitu dua belas rasi zodiak. Di antaranya terdapat tiga ratus enam puluh bintang dalam dua puluh satu gambar yang miring dari jalan Matahari ke arah utara. Di antaranya adalah Beruang Besar, Beruang Kecil, Naga, dan yang lainnya. Di antaranya terdapat tiga ratus enam belas bintang dalam lima belas gambar yang miring dari jalan Matahari. [UNCLEAR: pernyataan sumber tentang cara para ahli membagi bintang-bintang yang telah disebutkan sulit dipahami.]

Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Jabbār, yang dikenal melalui kitabnya [UNCLEAR: judulnya tampak sebagai “al-Baṣrah”] tentang bintang-bintang tetap, menyebutkannya dan berkata: Bintang-bintang dalam gambar-gambar utara mencakup Beruang Kecil. Bentuknya seperti beruang yang berdiri sambil merentangkan kedua kaki depannya. Ia memiliki tujuh bintang, dan orang-orang Arab menyebutnya Banāt Naʿsh Kecil. Empat bintang membentuk keranda dalam bentuk persegi, dan tiga berada pada ekornya. Delapan bintang berada di luar gambar. Di antaranya terdapat tujuh bintang yang oleh orang-orang Arab dikelompokkan sebagai Banāt Naʿsh Kecil, yaitu bintang-bintang yang diamati ke arah Kutub Utara. [UNCLEAR: uraian sumber yang tumpang tindih tentang hitungan tujuh dan delapan bintang dipertahankan sebagaimana disebutkan.]

Aku berkata: Di antaranya terdapat Beruang Besar dengan dua puluh tujuh bintang. Delapan bintang berada di luar gambar. Di antaranya ada tujuh bintang yang disebut orang-orang Arab Banāt Naʿsh: empat pada tubuhnya dan tiga pada ekornya. Orang-orang Arab menyebutnya al-Suhā. Di antaranya terdapat Naga dengan tiga puluh satu bintang. Bentuknya seperti ular besar dengan banyak lilitan. Bentuk itu dimulai dari empat bintang yang tersusun seperti persegi miring pada kepalanya. [UNCLEAR: frasa sumber setelah uraian tentang kepala dan kalajengking rusak.] Naga adalah suatu tempat di langit, sejenis ular, dan yang terbesar di antara mereka.

Di antaranya terdapat al-Fakkah, yang disebut Mahkota Utara. [UNCLEAR: sumber memberikan uraian rusak tentang sejenis ular di langit dan delapan bintang yang berkaitan dengan bentuknya yang bulat.] Al-Fakkah juga terdiri dari bintang-bintang bulat di belakang al-Simāk al-Rāmiḥ.

Di antaranya terdapat Sosok yang Berlutut, yang gambarnya memiliki dua puluh tujuh bintang. Di antaranya terdapat al-Sabʿāt, yang juga disebut al-Lawz dan al-Ṣubḥ al-Rūmī. Di antaranya terdapat Kura-kura, yang bintang-bintangnya berjumlah sepuluh; sebagian bintangnya digambarkan sebagai al-Nasr al-Wāqiʿ. Ada pula Ayam, yang memiliki sembilan belas bintang; dua bintang berada di luar gambar, dan bintang-bintangnya yang terbesar berada di Bima Sakti. Di antaranya terdapat Segitiga, yaitu empat bintang di antara bintang Ikan dan Elang di atas kepala al-Ghūl. Dengan demikian, jumlah gambar-gambar utara ini adalah tiga ratus enam puluh bintang.

Adapun gambar-gambar selatan berjumlah tiga ratus dua belas bintang. Di antaranya terdapat [UNCLEAR: Qayqaṭus] dengan dua puluh dua bintang. Bentuknya seperti hewan telanjang dengan dua kaki dan ekor seperti ekor ikan paus. Di antaranya terdapat al-Jabbār (Orion) dengan tiga puluh delapan bintang. Bentuknya seorang lelaki yang berlari sambil memegang tongkat, dengan sabuk dan pedang di bagian tengah tubuhnya. Di antara bintang-bintangnya terdapat al-Jawzāʾ, yaitu bintang merah. Ada pula dua belas bintang yang berkumpul di bawah kaki Orion, menyerupai kelinci yang wajahnya mengarah ke barat dan bagian belakangnya ke timur.

Di antaranya terdapat Anjing Besar dengan dua puluh delapan bintang; sebelas bintang berada di luar gambar, di belakang bintang-bintang al-Jawzāʾ. [UNCLEAR: hubungan antara al-Sunbulah dan bintang-bintang al-Shiʿrā al-ʿAbūr dalam sumber tidak jelas; sumber menyebut salah satunya al-Abbān al-Marzabān.] Di antaranya terdapat al-Shiʿrā al-Ghumaysāʾ, yaitu bintang-bintang yang terbit setelah al-Jawzāʾ. Adapun Cancer, [UNCLEAR: sumber menyebut gambar-gambar dalam al-Jawzāʾ dan al-Shiʿrā al-Ghumaysāʾ yang berada di lengan]. Orang-orang Arab menganggap bahwa keduanya adalah saudari-saudari Suhayl.

Di antaranya terdapat Mahkota Selatan dengan tiga belas bintang; enam bintang berada di luar gambar. Bentuknya seperti ikan besar, bintang-bintangnya berada di sebelah selatan bintang al-Dālī, kepalanya ke arah timur dan ekornya ke arah barat. Di antaranya terdapat Bima Sakti, [UNCLEAR: frasa lokasi dalam sumber rusak]. Inilah ringkasan bintang-bintang selatan dan utara.

Aku berkata: Apa yang disebutkan oleh sebagian penulis terbatas pada bintang-bintang yang masyhur. Adapun bintang-bintang yang kurang masyhur sangat banyak; bintang-bintang itu akan disebutkan kemudian, jika Allah Yang Mahatinggi menghendaki.

[Chapter on their bodies and what is connected to them]

Know that the Sun’s body is one hundred and a half times the measure of the world, and the Moon’s body is thirty-nine times the measure of the world. The same applies to Venus, Mercury, and Mars. Jupiter’s body is eighty-two times the measure of the world, and Saturn’s body is ninety-nine times the measure of the world. Some of our scholars said that the Sun’s body extends fifteen degrees before it and likewise behind it; the Moon’s body extends twelve degrees before it and likewise behind it; Mars’s body extends eight degrees behind it and likewise before it; Venus’s body extends seven degrees before it and likewise behind it; and Mercury’s body is likewise. God Most High, knows best.

[Chapter: every star in the heaven is many times the measure of the world]

As for the fixed stars, there are fifteen of them, including al-Shiʿrā al-ʿAbūr, al-Simāk, al-Nasr al-Ṭāʾir, Qalb al-Asad, and similar stars. Each of these stars is sixty-four times the measure of the world.

[Chapter on the seven stars traversing the spheres]

Know that the Moon traverses the sphere in twenty-nine days and one-third of a day; Mercury traverses it in twenty-eight days; Venus traverses it in two hundred and twenty-four days and one-quarter of a day; the Sun traverses it in three hundred and sixty-five days and one-quarter of a day; Mars traverses it in six hundred and thirty [UNCLEAR: the source omits the unit]; Jupiter traverses it in eleven years; and Saturn traverses it in twenty-nine years. God knows best.

[Chapter on the stations of the zodiac signs]

Know that the Moon’s station in each sign is two days and three nights; Mercury’s station in each sign is fifteen days; Venus’s station in each sign is twenty-five days; Jupiter’s station in each sign is one year; and Saturn’s station in each sign is thirty months.

[Chapter on the dignity of the planets]

Know that the Moon’s dignity is Taurus; Mercury’s dignity is Virgo; Venus’s dignity is Pisces; the Sun’s dignity is Aries; Mars’s dignity is Capricorn; Jupiter’s dignity is Cancer; and Saturn’s dignity is Libra. As for the Pleiades, it is said that they are the lamp of the world in the heaven because they are a gathering of stars like a knot. They are in the heaven, and the Arabs call them “the stars,” because there is no place in the heaven with more stars than them.

[Chapter on the day belonging to each of the seven planets]

Sunday belongs to the Sun; Monday to the Moon; Tuesday to Mars; Wednesday to Mercury; Thursday to Jupiter; Friday to Venus; and Saturday to Saturn.

[Chapter on the conjunction of the planets]

The meaning of conjunction is that one planet is in a sign while the other is in its counterpart. “Meeting” means that the two come together in one sign. Thus, by the command of God Most High, it influences every action. [UNCLEAR: the source then refers to this as being in the Qurʾan and says to understand it.]

When Saturn approaches Jupiter, wars spread throughout the regions, and a king from among the kings of the world and the earth dies. When Mars approaches Saturn, [UNCLEAR: the source says “that is what happens.”] When Saturn approaches the Sun, [UNCLEAR: the source again says “that is what happens.”] When Saturn conjoins Venus, it indicates high prices and drought. When Saturn conjoins Mercury, it indicates [UNCLEAR: the good condition of writing or the scribes]. When the Moon conjoins [another planet; the source omits the counterpart], it indicates the appearance of injustice in judgments. When Jupiter conjoins Mars, there are many hardships in the world.

[Chapter heading continues]

Mars is feminine, hot, and dry. It has yellow bile; its substance is iron and its taste is bitter. Its influence is over the head, the stomach, killing, women, and other things.

Jupiter is masculine, moderate, spiritual, and fortunate. It has blood; its substance is tin; its taste and color are white. Its influence is over the wind residing in the heart, and it brings abundant gifts and leadership.

Saturn is masculine, cold, dry, and dark. It has black bile; its substance is lead; its taste is bitter and its color black. Its influence is over study and deliberation, and it is associated with heat, injustice, subjugation, and coercion.

Apabila hari Jumat tiba, hendaklah ia mandi, pergi ke masjid jami, dan bersedekah dengan sesuatu. Setelah melaksanakan salat Jumat, hendaklah ia berkata: ‘Ya Allah, sesungguhnya aku memohon kepada-Mu dengan nama-Mu, Yang Maha Pengasih lagi Maha Penyayang: Allah, tiada tuhan selain Dia, Yang Hidup dan Yang Berdiri Sendiri, hingga akhir ayat—Dia yang di hadapan-Nya wajah-wajah tunduk, suara-suara merendah, dan hati-hati gentar karena takut kepada-Nya. Aku memohon kepada-Mu agar Engkau melimpahkan selawat dan salam kepada junjungan kami Muhammad, keluarganya, dan para sahabatnya, serta menunaikan hajatku, yaitu demikian dan demikian,’ lalu ia menyebutkan hajatnya.” Ia biasa berkata: “Jangan ajarkan hal itu kepada orang-orang bodoh di antara kalian, agar sebagian mereka tidak mendoakan keburukan atas sebagian yang lain lalu doa mereka dikabulkan seketika.”

Diriwayatkan dari Nabi, semoga Allah melimpahkan selawat dan salam kepadanya, bahwa beliau bersabda: “Jarak antara basmalah, ‘Dengan nama Allah Yang Maha Pengasih lagi Maha Penyayang,’ dan Nama Allah Yang Paling Agung hanyalah seperti jarak antara putihnya mata dan hitamnya.” Nabi, semoga Allah melimpahkan selawat dan salam kepadanya, juga bersabda: “Tidak ada pemisah antara manusia dan setan selain basmalah, ‘Dengan nama Allah Yang Maha Pengasih lagi Maha Penyayang.’ Ia adalah nama yang tersirat, yang menunjukkan bahwa apa yang sesudahnya adalah Nama Yang Paling Agung, yaitu Allah, karena Nama Yang Paling Agung adalah Nama Keagungan. Ia adalah poros segala nama dan semua nama kembali kepadanya. Di antara nama-nama, ia seperti nama diri: apabila engkau memohon dengan nama Yang Maha Pengasih, engkau berkata ‘Allah’; demikian pula nama-nama lainnya disandarkan kepadanya dan dikenal melalui keagungan serta ketinggian-Nya.

“Ia memiliki kemuliaan tambahan atas nama-nama lainnya: apabila engkau menghilangkan huruf alif darinya, tersisa ‘lillah’; apabila engkau menghilangkan lām pertama, tersisa ‘lah’; dan apabila lām kedua juga dihilangkan, tersisa ‘huwa’. Dengan demikian, setiap huruf darinya berdiri sendiri. Hal itu tidak berlaku pada nama-nama lain, karena apabila engkau menghilangkan satu huruf darinya, maknanya menjadi hilang. [UNCLEAR: sumber menyatakan bahwa huruf-huruf Nama Yang Paling Agung ini tidak berubah atau tidak rusak.] Ini merupakan kemuliaan atas nama-nama dan bukti bahwa ia adalah Zat yang dimuliakan, yang tetap memiliki kemuliaan dan kekekalan.

Yang Mahatinggi berfirman: ‘Serulah Allah atau serulah Yang Maha Pengasih; dengan nama mana pun yang kamu seru, Dia memberimu pilihan antara berkata “Wahai Allah” atau “Wahai Yang Maha Pengasih.”’

Among the special properties of Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm is that it is written at the beginning of every sūrah of the Noble Qurʾān. Among its special properties is that if a person recites it 786 times—the number the source associates with its letters—for seven consecutive days with an intention for a matter, he will obtain all of that: bringing good, warding off evil, or [UNCLEAR: the source says “the marriage of merchandise,” then says that it marries by the permission of God].

Among the special properties of Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm is that whoever recites it twenty-one times at bedtime will be protected by God Most High that night from accursed Satan, theft, and sudden death, and every affliction will be kept away from him.

Among its special properties is that if it is recited fifty times in the face of a tyrant, God Most High will humble him, cast its awe into that tyrant’s heart, and grant safety from his evil.

Among the special properties of Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm is that if it is recited at sunrise three hundred times while you face the Sun, together with invoking blessings upon the Prophet the same number of times, God Most High will provide for him from where he does not expect, and a year will not pass before he becomes completely wealthy.

Among the special properties of Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm for love and affection is that if it is recited over a cup of water 786 times and the water is given to whoever you wish, that person will love him intensely. If he drinks that water at sunrise for seven days, his dullness will disappear and he will retain everything he hears. [UNCLEAR: the source’s pronouns are ambiguous.]

Among the special properties of Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm is that if it is recited sixty-one times when rain falls, with the intention of seeking rain, God Most High will complete it. [UNCLEAR: the object of “complete it” is not specified.]

Among the special properties of Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm is that if it is recited after the dawn prayer two thousand five hundred times, with sincere intention and a humble heart, for forty days, God Most High will pour upon its reciter some of the hidden secrets. He will see in his sleep everything that occurs in the world. This requires spiritual discipline; he will see wonders, and he should keep his secret concealed.

Among the special properties of Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm for fulfilling needs and entering the presence of rulers is that whoever wants this should fast on Thursday, [UNCLEAR: the source says to “look upon oil and dates”], perform the sunset prayer, and recite it one hundred and twenty-one times. “By God, besides whom there is no deity, no man or woman carries it without becoming, in people’s eyes, like the full moon. He becomes honored, awe-inspiring, eminent, and obeyed. Everyone who sees him loves him, fulfills his need, and casts love for him into the hearts of creation.

If he writes it in a glass bowl forty times, erases it with Zamzam water or sweet well water, and drinks from that…”

Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, may God Most High have mercy on him, said concerning the meaning of His saying: {“When you mention your Lord alone in the Qur’an, they turn their backs in aversion”}: the meaning of that is Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm. And concerning His saying, {“He made them adhere to the word of piety, and they were most deserving of it and worthy of it”}, he said that it was Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm; and it was also said: “There is no deity except God.”

Whoever writes Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm and writes it beautifully, honoring it, will be recorded by God among those brought near. It is related from ʿIkrimah that he said: “God Most High existed and there was nothing with Him. Then God created the light, and from the light He created the Tablet and the Pen. Then God Most High commanded the Pen to write upon the Tablet what is to be. The first thing the Pen wrote on the Tablet was Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm. So God Most High made it a safeguard for His creation for whoever persists in reciting it. It is recited by the inhabitants of the seven heavens and the inhabitants of the pavilions of Paradise, including the cherubic angels, the truthful, and those who glorify God.

“The first thing sent down to Adam, peace be upon him, was Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm. He said: ‘Now I know that my descendants will not be punished by the Fire so long as they persist in reciting it.’ Then it was taken up after him until the time of Abraham, peace be upon him, and it descended upon him while he was in the catapult, so God Most High saved him from the Fire.

“Then it was taken up after him until the time of Solomon.
